shared_elements: tall upright stone monolith with roughly rectangular, slightly tapering silhouette
low-relief carving covering the whole front face
frontal anthropomorphic figure occupying the full height
circular/disc motifs on the torso area
horizontal banded element across the lower body (belt-like band)
paired vertical incised columns/strips in the upper zone
justification: Both are tall, slab-like stones carved on the front with a single frontal anthropomorphic figure organised in the same vertical order: an elaborated head/headgear zone at top with vertical strips, a torso bearing circular discs, and a horizontal band across the lower body. The manner of execution differs markedly, however: A is a very shallow, flat, almost linear relief on pale eroded stone where the imagery is barely legible, while B is a deeply modelled, bulky, three-dimensional carving in dark stone with pronounced rounded volumes.
